assignment_context:
Assignment Title: p1

Assignment Question:
A store applies a day's stock movements. Each movement names an item and a quantity, which is positive for a receipt and negative for an issue.
After all movements are applied, list every item whose net stock is greater than zero, in ascending order of item name, and report how many such items there are.
Design requirements (mandatory)
Ledger holds a HashMap<String,Integer> and exposes apply(String item, int qty), which accumulates the quantity for that item.
report() returns a Map<String,Integer> containing only the items with a positive net stock, already in ascending key order - use a TreeMap for this.
Use getOrDefault so no null check is needed.
Input format
Line 1: integer N - number of movements.
Next N lines: <item> <quantity>
Output format
One line per item with positive net stock, in ascending item order: <item> <stock>
Last line: ITEMS <number of such items>
Problem constraints
1 <= N <= 1000
Item name is 1 to 15 characters, no spaces
-100000 <= quantity <= 100000
Ordering is the natural String order, so uppercase sorts before lowercase
Notes
An item whose net stock ends at exactly zero is not listed.
An item may go negative in the middle of the day and recover, or the other way round - only the final total matters.
Sample input
6
PEN 100
BOOK 40
PEN -30
INK 25
BOOK -40
PEN 5
Sample output
INK 25
PEN 75
ITEMS 2

Here's the syntax:

```java

```

For your `Ledger` class using `HashMap<String, Integer>`:

```java
int currentQty = led.getOrDefault(item, 0);
```

This replaces the need for checking `if (led.get(item) != null)`.
